one_sentence_story: After a 1953 epilepsy operation removed Henry Molaison's medial temporal lobes on both sides, he kept his 118 IQ and childhood stories yet lost the ability to turn any passing moment into a lasting conscious memory.
so_what_for_you: Your conscious memory recorder only saves what holds undivided attention and sleep consolidation — if you multitask mid-conversation, the experience vanishes just like an interrupted rehearsal.
